headline: Which AI is best at research?
sig_plain: Check fifteen claims in a chief executive's all-staff email against the company's own records before it goes to 1,200 people, and fix the ones that are wrong.
sig_task:
From: Joanne Okafor, HR Director, Hollins Brook Foods
Date: Thursday 1 October 2026

Hi,

Martin (our CEO) wants to send the all-staff "People update" in `inputs/draft_message.md` on Monday. It goes to about 1,200 people, so every number in it has to be right. I've marked the fifteen claims to check as [C1] to [C15].

Everything I could pull together is in `inputs/docs/`: reports, emails, minutes and a few things from outside the company, written at different times over the last two years. Use only these documents. If they don't settle a claim, say so rather than guessing.

Please give me three files in `out/`:

**1. `out/briefing.md`: a one-page fact-check I can read in two minutes.**
- One line at the top with the totals, in the form "N supported, N wrong, N misleading, N cannot verify".
- Then a table with one row per claim, C1 to C15 in order, showing: the claim in a few words, the verdict, what the evidence says (with the correct figure if the claim is wrong), and at least one citation.
- Show each verdict as one of: ✔ Supported, ✘ Wrong, ⚠ Misleading, ? Cannot verify.
- No more than 600 words in total, citations included.

**2. `out/claims.json`: the same verdicts in this exact format.**

```json
{
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "C1",
      "verdict": "supported",
      "what_the_evidence_says": "One or two sentences.",
      "correct_figure": "The right figure or wording if the claim is wrong or misleading, otherwise null",
      "evidence": [
        {"doc": "d01_gpg_report_2024", "quote": "words copied exactly from that document"}
      ],
      "suggested_wording": "A replacement sentence for Martin, or null if the claim can stay as it is"
    }
  ]
}
```

`verdict` must be one of `supported`, `wrong`, `misleading`, `cannot_verify`:
- **supported**: the documents back the claim as written.
- **wrong**: the documents show it is false.
- **misleading**: true in a narrow sense, but staff would take away something false.
- **cannot_verify**: the documents don't contain enough to confirm or disprove it.

**3. `out/revised_message.md`: Martin's message, fixed.** Correct every figure the evidence lets you correct, and reword or remove anything we can't stand behind. Keep his voice and roughly the same length, don't add any new claims, and take out the [C] markers.

How to cite: in the briefing, put the document name and a short quote copied word for word, like this: `[d07_headcount_snapshot_2025_03: "Prepared by: HR Information team"]`. The name is the file name without `.md`. Each quote should be at least four words and copied exactly, so I can find it with a text search. In `claims.json`, put the same thing in the `evidence` list.

Thanks,
Joanne

premium_note.before: We tested both on every task in this lab. Neither scored higher than our best pick. Across all 25 tasks, Astra at medium thinking cost about four times as much as GPT-6.1 Sol at medium thinking. Both averaged 94 out of 100 across the six labs. Here are this lab's scores and costs:
premium_note.after:
### Why we don't recommend them

The personal versions of Claude and ChatGPT keep your chats, whichever model you choose. Some business services can be set up so the provider does not keep the data you send. A business account alone does not guarantee this.

Claude Fable has an extra requirement. Anthropic says: "Using Fable requires 30-day data retention for safety monitoring by default." That applies to business accounts too. Some eligible organisations can turn this retention off for a limited time. Fable has no option for processing data in the UK or EU.

Some providers make Fable optional. Harvey, which makes AI tools for law firms, says: "We are making this model available as an opt-in option vs. by default." Cursor, a popular coding tool, says Fable "is off by default in every Team that has Cursor Privacy Mode enabled and for every Enterprise customer". Jennifer Ellis, a lawyer who writes about legal technology, advises: "Don't use it if you have concerns about data retention or your firm has AI use policies against allowing data to be retained by outside tools."

So keep personal details, staff and customer records, unreleased figures, business plans and confidential findings out of Claude Fable. Check your organisation's AI policy before using it for work at all.

GPT-6 Astra has the same data retention rules as other OpenAI models. By default, OpenAI keeps records of use for up to 30 days to monitor misuse. Eligible customers can arrange for their data not to be kept in those records. Our reason for not recommending Astra is cost: with both set to medium thinking, Astra cost £8.87 and GPT-6.1 Sol cost £2.23 across all 25 tasks. Both averaged 94 out of 100 across the six labs.

### When a premium model is fine to use

If you need a lot of power for a long or difficult job, and none of the information is private or sensitive, a premium model is fine to use. Examples include researching a public topic in depth, working through published documents or completing a long coding task using code that isn't confidential. For Fable, Stephen Smith, who trains law firms to use AI, suggests asking: "can this engagement tolerate 30-day retention by the model provider? For a lot of work, the answer is yes. For some matters, it won't be."

For everyday work, start with a usual top model. Compare a premium model only if the results don't meet your needs.

To: All staff (email and noticeboards at all four sites)
From: Martin Ashdown, Chief Executive, Hollins Brook Foods Ltd
Planned send date: Monday 5 October 2026

---

Hello everyone,

Before the busy season starts, I want to share how we are doing as an employer. I am proud of these numbers, and they are yours.

**Fair pay.** Our median gender pay gap has fallen significantly in a year, from 14.2% to 7.4%, and our mean gap has fallen by a quarter. We have published our gender pay gap for the last two years as required by law. Women now hold 41% of our senior leadership roles, up from 35% a year ago.

**Pay.** In April, all frontline staff received a pay rise of 5%, reflecting their essential contribution to our business.

**A place people stay.** Voluntary staff turnover fell from 22.7% to 18.1% last year, well below the sector median of 20.4%. Sickness absence was 4.2%, slightly above the sector average of 3.6%.

**Growing.** Thorncliffe is now our fastest-growing site, and our Line 4 investment there has created 64 new jobs so far, with further expansion planned.

**Your voice.** Thank you to everyone who filled in the PulsePoint survey: four in five of you took part. Our engagement score rose four points this year to 72%.

**Learning.** We invested £362,500 in training and development last year.

Thank you for everything you do.

Martin
